ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, shareholders, senior management, and UBOs against: (1) the UN Security Council Consolidated List and FATF public statements; (2) the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) and Consolidated Non-SDN lists; (3) the EU and UK consolidated financial sanctions lists; (4) the South African terrorism and related activities list published by the Financial Intelligence Centre (FIC); screening frequency at pre-incorporation and on a continuous basis under Section 28A of FICA; enhanced due diligence trigger indicators include PEP status, FATF-identified jurisdictions, and cash-intensive business operations; risk classification for this entity: Low_Risk_Standard requiring standard CDD with UBO certification.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) e-Services portal (https://www.cipc.co.za), Company Registration module
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Section 11 of the Companies Act 71 of 2008 permits names in any of the 12 official South African languages; Latin-script transliteration of non-Latin names may be accepted with a sworn translation; the only mandatory transliteration requirement applies where a name is in an official language other than the primary language used by the incorporator; CIPC requires the suffix 'Proprietary Limited' or its abbreviation '(Pty) Ltd'; names must not be identical to an existing registered name and must not be confusingly similar to a pending name or a registered trademark per Section 11(2).
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon CIPC rejection, the applicant may: (1) resubmit an amended name application immediately through the CIPC e-services portal (no statutory cooling period); (2) file a formal reconsideration request with CIPC within 20 business days of rejection if procedural error is alleged; (3) appeal to the Companies Tribunal within 30 days under Section 7 of the Companies Regulations, 2011, or elect the Tribunal's alternative dispute resolution process; (4) as a final statutory remedy, apply to the High Court for judicial review under Section 164 of the Companies Act. Parallel remedy: if the rejection is based on trademark similarity, file a name-objection hearing or obtain a trademark coexistence/consent letter. All appeals must be accompanied by the CIPC rejection notice and the prescribed appeal fee.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted for the registered corporate office under Section 24 of the Companies Act 71 of 2008 (a registered office address must be a physical address within South Africa at which service of process may be effected; a virtual office service accommodating physical mail reception and service acceptance is generally accepted); however, the manufacturing site will require a separate physical industrial/commercial premises for SAHPRA establishment licensing under Regulation 6 of the Medical Devices and In Vitro Diagnostics Regulations (2020). A purely virtual office without mail-handling capacity will not satisfy CIPC compliance.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk: 40-55% likelihood of an unannounced or short-notice physical inspection within the first 12 months of operation, driven by SAHPRA's post-licensing GMP surveillance program, the local municipality's business licensing inspections, and the Department of Employment and Labour (occupational health and safety) random site visits; probability increases to >70% if any public complaints or import/export quality alerts are recorded.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 71 of 2008, ss 13–14 (incorporation), s 19 (legal personality), s 66 (board of directors); Companies Regulations 2011 (GNR 351 of 28 April 2011), Forms CoR 9.1 and CoR 14.1
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notice of Incorporation (CoR 14.1) together with the Memorandum of Incorporation (MOI)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up share capital for a Proprietary Limited Company under the Companies Act 71 of 2008; the sole subscriber may issue one or more shares for nominal consideration (commonly ZAR 1 per share). No escrow deposit or proof of capital payment is required at registration; the consideration for issued shares must be paid within 12 months or as provided in the MOI.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: That the incorporation of the Company be ratified and that the executed Memorandum of Incorporation and Notice of Incorporation (CoR 14.1) filed with CIPC be approved. RESOLVED FURTHER: That the subscription for 100 ordinary shares of no par value by the founding subscriber be accepted; that the shares be allotted and issued fully paid; and that the registered office be adopted at the address recorded in CoR 14.1, with the postal address confirmed. RESOLVED FURTHER: That [Name], ID [number], be appointed sole Director, that [Name] be appointed Chief Executive Officer, and that an independent auditor or accounting officer be appointed as required by section 84 or 85 of the Companies Act. RESOLVED FURTHER: That the Director and officers be jointly and severally authorised to execute all documents and open bank accounts to give effect to these resolutions.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Reservation and Pre-Approval Search
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) online customer portal (cipc.co.za)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register a customer account on the CIPC e-Services portal, conduct a name search against the CIPC company register, and submit Form CoR 9.1 to reserve two preferred proposed names. The reservation is valid for 6 months and is a prerequisite for submission of CoR 14.1.
required_dossiers: Completed CoR 9.1 (Application for Reservation of Name)
Identity document or passport of the applicant/director
Proof of CIPC customer registration (email verification)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a name is unavailable, file an alternative name application within the 6-month reservation period; if CIPC rejects the name for confusing similarity, file an amended CoR 9.1 with consent letters from existing name holders or a fresh name application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notice of Incorporation and MOI Submission
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) e-Services portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute the MOI, complete Form CoR 14.1 setting out the company type (Private Company), registered office, postal address, directors, and share count, and upload both forms with the prescribed issue fee. On acceptance, CIPC issues a Certificate of Incorporation assigning a registration number.
required_dossiers: Identities of first directors and alternate directors
Proof of registered office physical address (lease or title deed)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CIPC queries the filing, correct the indicated deficiencies (e.g., missing signature, incomplete MOI) and resubmit within the 20-business-day correction window; a rejected CoR 14.1 requires a fresh filing with a new CoR 9.1 if the name reservation lapses.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) Beneficial Ownership filing portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the Beneficial Ownership Register (Form CoR 5.1 / CoR 30.1 as applicable), identify all natural persons who directly or indirectly hold 5% or more of the beneficial interest, and file the register with CIPC together with the required declaration. CIPC will record the beneficial owners on the public register of the company.
required_dossiers: Certified identity documents of beneficial owners
Proof of indirect ownership chain (share certificates or trust deed)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CIPC issues a deficiency notice, supply missing supporting documentation or a sworn declaration from the beneficial owner; failure to lodge within 30 days of incorporation may expose the company to an administrative penalty, remedied by immediate filing and a letter of explanation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: SARS Income Tax and VAT Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS) via eFiling (sarsefiling.co.za)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receipt of the Certificate of Incorporation, register the company as a taxpayer with SARS using Form ITREG (for income tax) and, if annual taxable turnover exceeds ZAR 1 million, register for VAT on Form VAT101. Submit the company banking details and representative details; SARS issues an income tax reference number and, where applicable, a VAT number.
required_dossiers: Company bank account confirmation (e.g., confirmation letter from bank)
VAT101 registration form (if turnover exceeds statutory threshold)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SARS holds the registration for verification, provide the outstanding supporting documents within the prescribed grace period; where SARS delays the VAT number, escalate through the SARS branch office or seek a SARS Tax Clearance Status (TCS) interim letter to unblock supplier setup.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Employment and Labour (DoEL) – Unemployment Insurance Fund (UIF) and Compensation Fund (COIDA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register as an employer with the UIF via the uFiling portal or DoEL regional office using Form UI-8; simultaneously apply for a Compensation Fund registration under the Compensation for Occupational Injuries and Diseases Act using Form W.As.2 (Employer Registration). Registrations are prerequisite for lawful payroll operation.
required_dossiers: List of initial employees and projected payroll
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the UIF or Compensation Fund returns the application, correct mismatched names or payroll data and resubmit; provisional registration can be obtained pending submission of outstanding schedules. Late registration penalties can be disputed in writing with proof of timely attempt.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank Account Opening and Payment Rails Enablement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial bank of choice and Stripe South Africa (payment gateway)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a business current account in the company's name using the Certificate of Incorporation, MOI and the First Board Resolution. Provide bank confirmation to SARS. Thereafter, onboard the legal entity on Stripe with the company legal name, physical address and bank account details to enable credit card collection.
required_dossiers: First Board Resolution appointing authorised signatories
Certified IDs of directors and signatories
Proof of registered office and bank account application form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank rejects the application for insufficient KYC evidence, provide a full beneficial ownership register and sanctioned-person declarations; for Stripe rejections, provide a resolvable compliance questionnaire or submit a copy of the tax clearance certificate.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: South African Health Products Regulatory Authority (SAHPRA) and National Regulator for Compulsory Specifications (NRCS)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: SAHPRA Medical Device Establishment Licence (MDEL) and Class 1/Class 2 Medical Device Product Registration, together with an NRCS Letter of Authority if the product is subject to a compulsory specification relating to medical materials

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment (DFFE) – Provincial Environmental Affairs (via SAHPRA/GNR 327 EIA process)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Basic Assessment (Listing Notice 1, GNR 327) with an Atmospheric Emissions Licence (AEL) only if the thermoforming plant triggers a listed activity under Section 21 of the National Environmental Management: Air Quality Act 39 of 2004; small-scale thermoforming facilities compiling multilayer dental aligner sheets are generally a 'Registration Only' activity under Category 4.1 (plastic product manufacture) where VOC emissions are below 10 t per annum.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Air: NEMAQA (Act 39 of 2004) and National Dust Control Regulations (GNR 827) – VOC emissions must not exceed 40 mg/Nm3 as total organic compounds; odour and fume extraction must prevent nuisance emissions. Wastewater: municipal sewer by-laws (e.g., pH 6–10, TSS < 500 mg/L, COD < 1 500 mg/L, no free chlorine) and National Water Act 36 of 1998 s 21 permitting if any wastewater is discharged off-site. Solid waste: hazardous waste manifesting per National Environmental Management: Waste Act 59 of 2008 s 31 with strict separation of polyethylene terephthalate (PETG) trimming scrap from process solvents.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certificate from the local Fire Services Division under SANS 10400 Part T (National Building Regulations) for the manufacturing floor and solvent stores; structural load inspection certification by a professional engineer registered with the Council for the Built Environment; Electrical Certificate of Compliance (COC); Occupational Health and Safety Act 85 of 1993 compliance audit and Compensation Fund Certificate of Good Standing before commissioning the thermoforming and automated trimming line.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS); eFiling portal at https://www.sarsefiling.co.za; SARS Customs via the Customs and Excise Automated System (e.g., SAD 500 lodgement).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned South African (Pty) Ltd or non-resident company must: (1) appoint a public officer resident in South Africa; (2) register for income tax through SARS eFiling or a SARS branch using Form IT-TRAC/registration application, submitting the notarised certificate of incorporation, memorandum of incorporation, foreign company registration extract, and proof of physical address; (3) obtain an Income Tax Reference Number (ITREF) for the company; (4) if taxable supplies exceed or are expected to exceed the VAT threshold, lodge Form VAT 101 together with constitutional documents to obtain a VAT number; (5) register as an exporter with SARS Customs to obtain a Customs Code (DA 185 application) for export clearances of dental aligner sheets; (6) submit the relevant exchange control forms (e.g., Form NEP) to an authorised dealer in respect of export proceeds. Processing time is typically 1-3 business days for the ITREF and up to 21 business days for VAT registration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: South African law does not provide a 'check-the-box' pass-through election for a (Pty) Ltd; entity-level income tax applies mandatorily at 27% (years of assessment ending on or after 31 March 2023). Available elections and regimes relevant to a manufacturing (Pty) Ltd include: (i) VAT group registration election under section 50 of the VAT Act permitting commonly controlled companies to be treated as a single vendor; (ii) section 11D research and development allowance election (150% deduction for qualifying R&D expenditure); (iii) section 12R Special Economic Zone (SEZ) election granting a reduced 15% corporate tax rate for qualifying manufacturing operations located in a designated SEZ; (iv) section 9I headquarter company election for certain foreign-dividend and interest flows; (v) hybrid instrument classification is mandatory under sections 8F and 8M of the Income Tax Act and cannot be altered by election.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Compulsory registration threshold: ZAR 1,000,000 (actual or reasonably expected taxable turnover for any 12-month period); voluntary registration threshold: ZAR 50,000. Non-resident suppliers of imported services or goods supplied in South Africa are subject to reverse-charge rules and may have an obligation to register regardless of the threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: South Africa does not currently impose a mandatory real-time fiscal clearance or continuous transaction control (CTC) regime of the Brazilian NF-e type. SARS eFiling is the mandated digital channel for filing VAT 201 returns, and SARS Customs requires electronic lodgement of the SAD 500 export declaration. SARS has announced a phased adoption of a national e-invoicing framework aligned with the PEPPOL standard; however, e-invoicing remains voluntary as of the current effective date. Where e-invoices are used, they must satisfy the full or abridged tax invoice requirements of section 20 of the VAT Act, including the vendor's VAT number, invoice date, description of goods, quantity, and consideration; there is no digital stamp, tax clearance token, or server-side authorisation requirement for invoice validity. SARS retains the right to validate invoice data and cross-match export declarations, bills of lading, and bank receipts.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating under section 11(1)(a)(i) of the VAT Act applies where the company supplies goods (including multilayer thermoplastic dental aligner sheets classifiable under HS 3920/3921 or as medical devices in accordance with SARS tariff rulings) to a person who is not a resident of South Africa and the goods are exported from South Africa within 90 days of the time of supply (as prescribed by SARS Interpretation Note 30). Alternatively, zero-rating may apply where the supplier is a vendor and the goods are delivered by the vendor to a licensed customs and excise exporter for direct export. For services, section 11(2)(l) zero-rates services supplied to non-residents who are outside South Africa at the time of supply, unless the services are physically rendered in South Africa or are directly connected to immovable property or movable property situated in South Africa. The exporter must obtain and retain documentary proof of export, including the SAD 500 declaration, transport documents, and payment evidence, before any refund is paid. Foreign exchange proceeds must be repatriated to South Africa through an authorised dealer; the standard statutory requirement is receipt within 30 days from the date of export, and any extension requires prior approval from the South African Reserve Bank or an authorised dealer.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: SAD 500 Customs Export Declaration (electronic SARS Customs clearance)
Bill of Lading or Airway Waybill
Certificate of Origin (SACU format) or EUR.1 Movement Certificate where applicable
Bank Foreign Exchange Export Form (NEP) and Inward Remittance Certificate or bank advice evidencing receipt of export proceeds
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: SARS may re-open a zero-rated export claim within the five-year prescription period; if the goods are not physically exported within 90 days of the time of supply, or the requisite documentary proof is not produced, the supply is deemed taxable at 15% and the net VAT becomes due with interest. Additional tax under section 60 of the VAT Act may be imposed at up to 200% of the VAT shortfall where the incorrect zero-rating was made knowingly or without reasonable care. The Tax Administration Act 28 of 2011 imposes understatement penalties ranging from 10% (reasonable care) to 150% (intentional tax evasion) of the shortfall under section 223. Criminal liability arises under section 234 of the Tax Administration Act for fraudulent or materially false export declarations, carrying fines or imprisonment up to ten years. SARS also operates a dedicated export verification unit that scrutinises high-value medical device exports; any clawback will include statutory interest at the prescribed rate per section 76 of the VAT Act, and repeat offenders face enhanced audit ratings and possible real-time clearance monitoring.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: South African Reserve Bank (SARB) — Financial Surveillance Department (FinSurv), acting under the Currency and Exchanges Act, 1933 and the Exchange Control Regulations, 1961; operational authority is delegated to Authorised Dealers (registered banks) and Authorised Dealers in Foreign Exchange with Limited Authority.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: ZAR is fully convertible on the current account: bona fide trade payments, service fees, royalties, interest, dividends and branch profits may be remitted through an Authorised Dealer without prior SARB approval, subject to documentary verification and SARS tax compliance (profit remittance additionally requires satisfaction of the Companies Act solvency/liquidity test and accounting for the 20% dividends tax, or a treaty-reduced rate). The capital account is selectively convertible: inward direct investment and qualifying inward loans require no prior approval but must be reported and recorded as inward-listed capital so that future dividend and capital repatriation rights are preserved; outbound capital transfers by residents are restricted and require FinSurv approval or use of a permitted Authorised Dealer channel. ZAR is not internationalised: offshore ZAR deposit and ZAR NDF markets are available only to non-resident counterparties, and onshore entities must settle exclusively through Authorised Dealers.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export proceeds must be repatriated into the South African banking system within 180 days from the date of shipment, as applied by FinSurv through the Authorised Dealer community. There is no mandatory conversion ratio: 100% of the declared export value may be credited to a Foreign Currency Account (FCA) or Export Retention Account (ERA) held with an Authorised Dealer, and only proceeds not retained in such accounts must be sold for ZAR. The exporter must submit the commercial invoice, transport documents, customs SAD500 export declaration and proof of receipt to the Authorised Dealer, which tracks the 180-day cycle on the SARB Excon system and requires prior approval for any extension.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 business days following each anniversary of the company's incorporation date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing administrative penalty ZAR 100–500 depending on turnover tier; two consecutive years of non-compliance trigger CIPC notice of final deregistration (strike-off) and director disqualification.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial Ownership Annual Confirmation and updated Beneficial Ownership Register (s26A–26C, Companies Act 2008 as amended 2022)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually, filed simultaneously with the Annual Return (within 30 business days of incorporation anniversary); any change in beneficial ownership must be filed within 10 business days of the change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal offence carrying fine or imprisonment up to 10 years; administrative penalties up to ZAR 1 million; CIPC suspension of compliance status blocking annual returns and share transfer registrations.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (ITR14) with audited/reviewed AFS attached
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 12 months after financial year-end; provisional tax returns and payments due at the six-month midpoint of the financial year, at year-end, and as a top-up within 6–7 months after year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing administrative penalty ZAR 250–8,000 per month (turnover-based); understatement penalty of 10–150% of the tax shortfall; daily statutory interest on unpaid tax; escalation to criminal prosecution and director personal liability.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Medical Device Establishment Licence annual renewal and annual notification (dental aligner manufacturing/import)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: South African Health Products Regulatory Authority (SAHPRA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually, on or before the licence anniversary date, with current quality-management and product documentation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Expiry immediately suspends lawful manufacture, import, export and distribution of clear-aligner products; SAHPRA administrative fines, licence withdrawal, product recall and responsible-person prohibition may follow.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Statutory audit is compulsory where the Public Interest Score (PI) is 350 or more; PI 100–349 requires independent review; PI below 100 may be exempted only where all members are directors and unanimously consent in writing. PI (Companies Act s26(3)): 1 point per employee, 1 point per ZAR 1m of turnover, 1 point per ZAR 1m of third-party liabilities, 10 points per individual with a beneficial interest in shares. Public companies and state-owned companies are always audited.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS for companies with public accountability or PI ≥ 350; IFRS for SMEs is acceptable for other Pty Ltd companies. AFS must be prepared within 6 months of financial year-end (s30, Companies Act 2008) and present fairly per s29.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The company must maintain a Beneficial Ownership Register and file the Beneficial Ownership Annual Confirmation with CIPC together with each Annual Return. Share transfers or any change in ultimate beneficial ownership must be recorded and filed with CIPC within 10 business days of the change. CIPC blocks acceptance of the Annual Return and share-transfer filings while UBO records are outstanding.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Beneficial Ownership (s26A, Companies Act 2008 as amended)
Minute Book (shareholders, board and committee resolutions)
Register of Auditors / Independent Reviewer (s24 and s85, Companies Act 2008)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 160–430 (ZAR 3,000–8,000) per annum for registered office, company secretarial support and CIPC annual compliance handling
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Independent review (PI 100–349): USD 540–1,600; full statutory audit (PI ≥ 350): USD 2,700–8,100 (ZAR 50,000–150,000) for a mid-sized manufacturer

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general statutory tax holiday for a standard Pty Ltd; preferential tax expenditures apply: Section 12C capital allowance on manufacturing machinery (thermoforming and trimming equipment), Section 11D research and development deduction (150% of qualifying expenditure), Section 12H learnership allowance, and Section 12B renewable energy allowance. A reduced 15% corporate tax rate is available only to qualifying enterprises in designated Special Economic Zones (SEZs), subject to the enforcement of SEZ regulatory requirements.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Indefinite (no statutory expiry for assessed losses; subject to continuity-of-business and change-in-ownership limitation rules)

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: ITR14 (Company Income Tax Return) submitted via SARS eFiling at www.sarsefiling.co.za; provisional tax estimates are submitted on the IRP6 return through the same eFiling portal or accredited tax software.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual final return plus two provisional IRP6 returns per year of assessment; the final ITR14 reconciles all provisional tax payments, PAYE credits, foreign tax credits, and withholding taxes.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The ITR14 must be filed within 12 months after the financial year-end, unless SARS prescribes an earlier effective due date. Provisional IRP6 first payment is due on the last day of the sixth month from the start of the year of assessment; the second provisional payment is due on the last day of the year of assessment. For a standard February year-end, this means 31 August and 28 February.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: SARS income tax reference number and company registration number.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident company must first register for South African tax and enter the issued SARS tax reference; a foreign company number and country of incorporation are also required.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, trading name, registered business address, and postal address.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide the South African registered office or appointed representative address; when operating through a branch, disclose the branch address and the SARS-appointed responsible person.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Year of assessment and financial period start and end dates.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident branch uses the branch's annual accounting period, which must align with the parent's year unless SARS permits otherwise.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross local turnover and gross income from South African source operations, including all sales of dental clear aligner sheets and related intra-group supply fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include only South African-source income and foreign income attributable to a South African permanent establishment; offshore sales booked outside the PE remain outside the ITR14 scope.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Exempt income and reconciliation items (e.g., qualifying foreign dividends, foreign branch income excluded by treaty).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Exemptions are allowed only if the income is not effectively connected to a South African PE; supporting transfer pricing and residency documentation must be retained.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductions: cost of sales (polymer sheets, aligner film, thermoforming consumables), manufacturing overheads, staff costs, repairs, rent, interest, royalties, depreciation, and capital allowances.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deductions are strictly allowable only to the extent they are incurred in producing taxable income attributable to the South African operation; an apportionment memorandum for head-office overheads is required.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Assessed loss brought forward from prior tax year, supported by an assessed-loss schedule.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident branch may carry forward losses only if the same trade continues and there is no disqualifying change in ownership or business model.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income or assessed loss for the current year after applying all deductions, exemptions, and capital allowances.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Treaty provisions do not reduce the current-year taxable income; they allocate taxing rights between states. CFC disclosures and branch income allocations must be attached.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Income tax payable at 27% (or 15% for an applicable SEZ-qualifying enterprise) before foreign tax credits and other rebates.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident branch profits are taxed at 27% at the South African branch level; there is no separate branch-profits tax on remittances to the foreign head office.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Provisional tax paid (IRP6), foreign tax credits, dividend withholding tax credits, and PAYE credits claimed against the tax assessed.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident companies may claim foreign tax credits only against South African tax on the same foreign income, supported by direct foreign tax assessment certificates.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Balance of tax due or refund due, with bank account details for electronic transfer.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident must provide a South African bank account for any refund; if no local account exists, extended verification and a beneficial-owner declaration are required before SARS releases the refund.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of the ITR14 triggers an administrative non-compliance penalty of 10% of the assessed tax per month (with a maximum of 100%), interest at the prescribed rate (currently 9% per annum), and an understatement penalty of up to 200% where the late return understates taxable income. SARS may also issue a default assessment based on estimated income, which the taxpayer must then contest with full evidence.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 20% (South African dividends tax on non-resident shareholders, effective for dividends declared on or after 22 February 2017; previously 15%).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To obtain a reduced dividend withholding tax rate under an applicable Double Taxation Agreement (DTA), the non-resident beneficial owner must submit to the withholding agent, prior to the dividend payment, a completed SARS DTR01 declaration together with a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by its country of residence. The declaration confirms treaty entitlement, beneficial ownership, and the relevant DTA article. If the documents are not provided by payment date, the paying company must withhold at 20% and the non-resident may file a refund claim through SARS eFiling (DTR02 process) within three years of the overpayment.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory withholding tax rate is 15%; DTA-protected royalties are commonly reduced to 10% or 0% depending on treaty terms. Interest: statutory withholding tax rate is 15%; DTA rates generally range from 0% to 10%, with lower rates commonly available for professional or bank interest paid to treaty-resident financial institutions.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation (Local File and Master File) is required for all cross-border connected-person transactions regardless of a single monetary threshold; the SARS Transfer Pricing Disclosure Return (IT2) becomes mandatory when the taxpayer's annual gross receipts equal or exceed ZAR 100 million; Country-by-Country Reporting applies to multinational groups with consolidated annual revenue of ZAR 10 billion or more.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: South Africa does not have standalone Economic Substance Regulations comparable to those in the UAE or the Cayman Islands; instead, economic substance is an embedded statutory and judicial principle enforced through the general anti-avoidance provisions (ss 80A–80L of the Income Tax Act), the controlled foreign company attribution rules (s 9D), and transfer pricing accurate delineation principles. A Pty Ltd manufacturing dental clear aligners must demonstrate real operational substance — physical factory premises, engaged employees, actual raw-material purchasing, and decision-making functions in South Africa — to support its tax residency, treaty benefits, and deductibility of cross-border payments.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately under-declaring taxable turnover, fabricating raw-material invoices, or double counting deductions in the ITR14 (e.g., materially overstated polymer sheet purchases for clear aligner thermoforming).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: SARS issues a revised assessment with the omitted tax, interest at the prescribed rate, and an understatement penalty of up to 200% of the shortfall. Criminal conviction under section 235 of the Tax Administration Act exposes the company and participating officers to a fine of up to ZAR 10 million and/or imprisonment of up to 10 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly participate in the fraud may be treated as responsible persons under section 169 of the Tax Administration Act and be held jointly and severally liable for the company's unpaid tax; asset restraint orders, travel bans, and disqualification from directorship are statutory consequences.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Misstatement and Thin Capitalisation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Structuring aligner sheet sales to a foreign affiliate at below arm's-length prices, paying excessive royalty or interest to a connected person in a low-tax jurisdiction, failing to file the IT2 Transfer Pricing Disclosure Return, or failing to maintain contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: SARS adjusts the taxable income to reflect arm's-length conditions, disallows the excessive deduction, imposes interest, and levies an understatement penalty determined by grade — up to 200% for intentional or highly culpable misstatements. Failure to submit the IT2 return and TP documentation triggers administrative non-compliance penalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approved or knowingly ignored the mispricing can be cited as responsible persons for the additional corporate tax; in cases of gross negligence, they face personal liability, disqualification, and civil recovery proceedings in the High Court.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the Pty Ltd as a letterbox entity with no production plant or employees in South Africa, routing clear aligner royalty streams or supply-chain profits through a no-tax jurisdiction, and relying on a DTA for dividend or interest relief without substantive business activity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: SARS cancels the tax benefit under the general anti-avoidance rule (section 80B), recomputes tax as if the arrangement had not been entered into, and adds an understatement penalty of up to 200% plus interest; treaty benefits are denied under the principal purposes test.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A court may pierce the corporate veil where the arrangement was a sham, holding shareholders and directors personally liable for the corporate tax debt; directors also face civil restitution claims for breach of fiduciary duty and possible travel bans under the Tax Administration Act.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to file the annual ITR14 and both provisional IRP6 returns for two or more fiscal years; failing to register for income tax, VAT, or PAYE despite operating a profitable aligner manufacturing business with employees.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: SARS raises a default assessment based on estimated taxable income; late filing penalties accumulate monthly (10% per month of assessed tax, capped at 100%); interest compounds; criminal prosecution may follow for habitual non-compliance under section 234 of the Tax Administration Act.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be issued with personal liability notices for outstanding PAYE and provisional tax debts where the company has ceased trading or been liquidated without settlement; directors can be prohibited from leaving South Africa until the debt is resolved or security is provided.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the aligner sales platform (including Stripe and credit-card rails) without FICA-compliant customer due diligence; failing to file cash threshold reports or suspicious transaction reports; processing transactions for sanctioned dental providers or for criminal proceeds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Non-compliance with the Financial Intelligence Centre Act (FICA) carries administrative penalties of up to ZAR 10 million per contravention and criminal liability: imprisonment of up to 15 years and/or fines for responsible officers. SARS may also invoke anti-money-laundering audit powers to assess hidden income with penalties up to 200%.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, as accountable-institution management, are personally liable for FICA failures attributable to negligence or willful blindness; upon conviction they face imprisonment, travel bans, prohibitions on directing any financial business, and civil restitution for any laundered funds.
